provenanceNote: All content original paraphrase. No verbatim text from published book. All scenarios invented fresh.

frameworks.definition: The default orientation: I already know what is true, and the purpose of this conversation is to get you to accept it. Structurally fails because the other person has their own internally coherent version and is not waiting for yours.

The alternative orientation: the purpose of this conversation is to understand what each person sees, what each is missing, and what might change once both people see more. Not agreement — a different goal.

anchors.label: The co-founders' roadmap fight
anchors.description: Two co-founders arguing over product roadmap with same data, each pushing harder each week without asking what the other sees.
anchors.concreteDetail: Same spreadsheet in every meeting, no new data
anchors.friction: Each push makes the other dig in harder
anchors.sourceLocation: Invented fresh; supported by diff-conv.txt Ch2 co-founders reference

anchors.label: The design feedback loop
anchors.description: Team lead delivering same feedback three times in three different framings, designer responding consistently each time.
anchors.concreteDetail: Three framings: question, direct statement, company policy
anchors.friction: Framing change doesn't change stance; designer reads each as same message
anchors.sourceLocation: Invented fresh; supported by Ch2 teaching implication

anchors.label: The household argument
anchors.description: Couple having same household labor argument for six weeks; both have lists, neither has asked what it feels like from the other side.
anchors.friction: Each explanation received as same old argument

limits: The learning stance depends on the other person also being willing to have a conversation rather than a confrontation
The learning stance can be performed without being real — and the other person can tell the difference
Genuinely entering the learning stance and hearing the other person fully does not guarantee agreement or convergence
The learning stance can be weaponized as strategic humility that extracts information without genuine openness
unsupportedZones: When to let go of the conversation entirely (Ch07)
Any suggestion that the learning stance is sufficient for all difficult conversations
